articles.title: Pakistan vs England: Shadab Khan makes maiden ODI century in 89-run last wicket stand to secure victory despite Ben Duckett ton
articles.summary: Pakistan put on an incredible 89-run last-wicket stand to beat England, who suffered third successive defeat; watch England's next ODI in the tri-series against Sri Lanka live on Sky Sports Cricket on Thursday, coverage stars from 7:30am (first ball 8am)
articles.body:
Ben Duckett made an impressive 105 off 111 for his fifth ODI century, but his innings was the lone bright spot in an otherwise disappointing batting performance from England, who were limited to a below-par total of 241 all out after 46.4 overs thanks in large part to the impressive bowling of Shaheen Shah Afridi (4-46).

England's bowlers then decimated Pakistan's top order with Jamie Overton (3-43) impressive and Liam Dawson (2-19) relentless, as the hosts slipped to 154-9 having been 74-3.

All hope appeared lost for Pakistan with one wicket remaining, but Shadab - alongside the impenetrable No 11 Haris Rauf (7no off 19) - notched his career-best ODI score and his maiden century to guide his side to a victory made even more dramatic by a successful DRS review when Shadab was given out lbw to Atkinson on 97.

Shadab and Rauf's partnership was the highest last-wicket stand in a successful run chase in ODI history, and secured Pakistan's place in the tri-series final.

The win is England's second heartbreaking defeat in a row - after Sri Lanka recorded the second-highest successful run chase In ODI history against them on Thursday - and means that England must win against Sri Lanka to have any chance of a place in the final, with their last group-stage match live on Sky Sports from 7:30am on Thursday.

How Shadab led Pakistan to unfathomable comeback victory

England's bid to end their barren run of defeats in the tri-series got off to the worst possible start, with in-form opener Banton (4) chipping tamely to Arafat for Shaheen's 150th ODI wicket, before the Pakistan captain struck again with an almost mirrored dismissal of Root (5), who was caught after an uncharacteristically careless slash into the off-side.

Things went from bad to worse for the tourists when ODI debutant Razaullah - who notched an unforgettable 81 off 63 in the third Test against England at Edgbaston in August - fired a brilliant throw into the keeper and ran out Brook to leave England reeling at 19-3.

Despite the dismissal of Jordan Cox (6) at the end of the poweplay, Duckett began to lead a resurgence for England, building an impressive 93-run stand with Sam Curran (42 off 52) on his way to his second century in Lahore after his career-best 165 against Australia in 2025 - to bring England back to 145-5 having been 52-4.

Curran's dismissal, though, was the first of a flurry of wickets for Pakistan that saw Duckett out on 105 and England fall from 175-6 to 201-9.

Atkinson (36no) attempted to raise the pace, blasting three sixes in a 40-run last-wicket partnership with debutant Henry Crocombe, but the latter's dismissal consigned England to a below-par total of 241.

Brook's side started quickly with the ball, as Atkinson and Crocombe dismissed Fakhar Zaman (10), Saim Ayub (6), and Babar Azam (10) in 13 powerplay deliveries to give England hope.

A brief Pakistan resurgence led by the impressive Saad Baig (32) was ended by standout bowler Overton - the first of his three wickets - before the dismissal of Hasan Nawaz (15) and Arafat Minhas (1) in the space of three balls left the home side reeling at 103-6 after just 23.1 overs.

All hope seemed lost for Pakistan when Razaullah's (8) wicket put England on the brink of victory, with their opponents stranded with one wicket left and a deficit of 88 runs.

Shadab, whose ensuing heroics saw him smash 12 fours and four maximums, thought his innings was over when the umpire raised the finger after Gus Atkinson's yorker trapped him in front, going as far as to shake hands with his opponents during the review, only for DRS to reveal the faintest of inside edges to keep Pakistan's talisman at the crease.

Pakistan were then 20 runs away, and it was the unlikely hero Rauf who produced a picturesque drive down the ground for the winning boundary that gave his team the most unfathomable of victories with 2.5 overs to spare.

England captain Harry Brook, speaking at the presentation:

"I don't think it went wrong with the ball, to be honest. I thought we did an exceptional job to restrict them to us nearly winning the game.

"We probably didn't quite get enough runs on the board, but the effort the boys put in with the ball and in the field was phenomenal.

"Ben Duckett played an exceptional innings - his fifth ODI hundred which came at a good time.

"He played really well and that partnership that he and Sam Curran had together put us in a decent position to kick on.

"Unfortunately we lost a few wickets in quick succession but the way that Gus Atkinson finished the innings off was awesome."

Shaheen: I've never seen an innings like that in my life!

Pakistan captain Shaheen Shah Afridi, speaking at the presentation:

"The way Shadab Khan and Haris Rauf finished the game with the bat - I have never seen in my life an innings like that.

"I am really happy as a captain. Starting with the bowling, the team effort was top-drawer.

"We thought we had a lot of variation in the team so that's why we brought Shadab in.

"[But] we need top-order runs, we're struggling. I hope the next few games we'll bring that energy."

Watch England's next tri-series match, against Sri Lanka in Lahore, live on Sky Sports Cricket and Main Event from 7.30am on Thursday (8am first ball). Not got Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals or stream with no contract through NOW - cancel anytime.

articles.title: Deepti Sharma creates history, becomes first Indian woman to score ODI ton at No. 6 or lower
articles.summary: Deepti Sharma scripted history with a magnificent unbeaten century against Zimbabwe in the second women's ODI in Vadodara on Sunday, becoming the first
articles.body: Deepti Sharma scripted history with a magnificent unbeaten century against Zimbabwe in the second women's ODI in Vadodara on Sunday, becoming the first Indian woman to score an ODI hundred while batting at No. 6 or lower. The all-rounder struck an unbeaten 106 off 86 balls to surpass Richa Ghosh's previous record of 94 against South Africa in Visakhapatnam last year.Deepti's 83-ball century powers IndiaDeepti reached her century in 83 balls, making it one of the quickest ODI hundreds by an Indian woman. Her knock featured 15 boundaries and helped India maintain the momentum in the closing stages of the innings.The century also placed Deepti among India's fastest ODI centurions, with only Smriti Mandhana and Harmanpreet Kaur having registered quicker hundredsQuickest ODI hundreds for India Women (by balls):50 balls – Smriti Mandhana vs Australia, Delhi, 202570 balls – Smriti Mandhana vs Ireland, Rajkot, 202577 balls – Smriti Mandhana vs Australia, Mullanpur, 202582 balls – Harmanpreet Kaur vs England, Chester-le-Street, 202583 balls – Deepti Sharma vs Zimbabwe, Vadodara, 2026*Deepti's effort was particularly significant given her position in the batting order. Coming in lower down, she balanced the need to build an innings with the urgency to score quickly, finishing unbeaten to give India a strong total.Harmanpreet, Deepti set record partnershipDeepti's century was complemented by a superb 126 off 121 balls from Harmanpreet Kaur, who also reached a significant milestone during the innings. Harmanpreet's eighth ODI hundred took her past Mithali Raj's tally of seven, making her India's second-highest century-maker in women's ODIs behind Smriti Mandhana.The pair stitched together a 153-run partnership, setting a new Indian women's ODI record for the highest stand for the fifth wicket or lower. They surpassed the previous record of 122 runs, shared by Sneh Rana and Pooja Vastrakar against Pakistan at the 2022 Women's World Cup.India eventually finished on 328/6, setting Zimbabwe a target of 329 in the second ODI.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Pakistan vs England: Shadab Khan condemns Harry Brook's side to another improbable loss
articles.summary: England somehow lose another one-day international from a seemingly unbeatable position thanks to an improbable last-wicket stand by Pakistan in Lahore.
articles.body:
One-day international tri-series, Lahore

England 241 (46.4 overs): Duckett 105 (111), Shaheen 4-46

Pakistan 243-9 (47.1 overs) : Shadab 113* (96), Overton 3-43

England somehow lost another one-day international from a seemingly unbeatable position thanks to an improbable last-wicket stand by Pakistan in Lahore.

Three days after conceding 430 to lose to Sri Lanka, Harry Brook's side were beaten despite reducing Pakistan to 154-9 in pursuit of 242.

Shadab Khan was the engineer of Pakistan's unlikely win, striking a quite brilliant unbeaten 113 - the highest score by a number eight in an ODI.

He was supported by Haris Rauf, Pakistan's number 11 contributing seven to the unbroken 10th-wicket partnership of 89 - comfortably a new record for a last-wicket pair to win an ODI.

In barely believable scenes, Shadab was given out lbw to Gus Atkinson on 97, with 21 runs still required.

The players shook hands before Shadab called for a speculative review. DRS found a tiny inside edge and, reprieved, he watched Rauf belt debutant Henry Crocombe down the ground for the winning boundary with 17 balls to spare.

It means England are all but out of the tri-series - their exit will be confirmed if Sri Lanka beat Pakistan on Tuesday.

A second implosion in as many matches is hugely concerning for England, who looked to be on course for victory despite being bowled out for only 241.

Ben Duckett made a fine 105 - only the opener, Sam Curran and Gus Atkinson passing 20 in blameless conditions.

Nevertheless, England were well on course thanks to a collectively relentless display from their bowlers. Jamie Overton bowled his 10 overs in one spell for 3-43.

Then came Shadab and another baffling defeat for England, who could be out before they play their final game against Sri Lanka on Thursday.

Unbelievable last-wicket stand beats England

Tournament experience teaching England to lose

With less than a year to go to the World Cup, this tri-series was designed to give England experience of the pressure and permutations of tournament play.

In a matter of days, they have gone through two extreme situations, both ending in crushing defeats. What linked both matches was England's powerlessness to salvage the situation once the momentum turned against them.

If anything, the finish to this match was more dramatic than Sri Lanka pulling off the second-highest chase in ODI history .

Even Shadab was convinced he was out when he was hit on the shin by Atkinson's low full toss - he called for the hopeful review as he was walking off the field. When it came back in his favour, he put his head in his hands and was embraced by Rauf.

In the heat of the tight finish, Rauf had to be pulled away from a confrontation with England's Will Jacks when a Sam Curran bouncer was not called wide, while Rauf could also have been run out by Tom Banton's flick from mid-on when 18 were still required.

Shadab expertly farmed the strike - Rauf faced only 19 deliveries in a stand that lasted 80 balls.

Rauf defended his first 18 balls then cut loose to his 19th, hammering Crocombe for four then running away and throwing his bat in the air to begin the joyous celebrations.

What must England do to win a match in this tri-series? They have lost all three of their matches, the past two in extraordinary circumstances.

Yes, England are without key players Jofra Archer, Jos Buttler and Jacob Bethell on this tour, while Adil Rashid has been omitted from the XI and Josh Tongue missed out with a toe injury.

Still, what they are learning is they do not respond well in tight situations. On Thursday, the batters broke records, only to be let down by the bowlers. On Sunday, the bowlers were on course to mask the deficiencies of the batters, then wilted when it mattered.

This loss means encouraging performances from Duckett and Overton will be forgotten. For Duckett, this was a much-needed score at time when questions have been asked about his position. Overton was superb, the first England seamer to bowl 10 consecutive overs in an ODI since 2017.

But, when England needed inspiration to take the last wicket, they were found wanting. Maybe the pace of Archer or Tongue, or mystery of Rashid would have made the difference.

They crowded the bat for Rauf, tried to defend against Shadab and held countless meetings. Heads dropped, plans failed and England were not good enough.

To focus only on England does a disservice to Shadab, who played a knock for the ages, one of the greatest by a Pakistan batter in an ODI.

The all-rounder had been left out of the first two matches of this series. After bowling seven overs with his leg-spin, he arrived to bat when his team were in disarray at 103-6, then left as a hero.

Shadab was unflappable in the face of such a monumental task, supported by the fiery Rauf. In a 96-ball stay, Shadab expertly picked his moments to attack, pouncing when England erred. He hit five sixes and 13 fours.

Rauf batted for 70 minutes, more than two times his previous longest stay in an ODI. Only once before had he faced more deliveries.

As tension rose, so did the tempers - Joe Root had to step in to guide Rauf away from Jacks.

Rauf had the last word, but this will be remembered as Shadab's match.

articles.title: Shadab Khan and Haris Rauf  pull off miracle with record 89-run partnership for last wicket as Pakistan stun England in Lahore
articles.summary: The game looked set for England when Haris Rauf walked out to bat at number 11 with Pakistan at 154 for 9 in their chase of 242, still needing 88 runs to
articles.body: The game looked set for England when Haris Rauf walked out to bat at number 11 with Pakistan at 154 for 9 in their chase of 242, still needing 88 runs to win.It looked like it was all over, and England certainly thought so. But Shadab Khan, who came in at number eight, did the unthinkable, stitching together an unbeaten 89-run partnership for the last wicket with Rauf to take Pakistan home in Lahore on Sunday. in the fourth ODI of the tri-series, which also features Sri Lanka.Shadab chipped away at the target, finding a boundary in almost every over while managing to keep the strike with himself most of the time. Rauf played his part too, defending when needed and ducking and weaving as England threw everything at him. He hung in there to finish unbeaten on seven, while Shadab dictated terms at the other end. Rauf eventually hit the winning runs and raced away with his arms raised.The unbeaten 89-run stand between Shadab and Rauf is now the highest for the 10th wicket in a successful ODI chase. The previous record was an unbeaten 64-run partnership between Deryck Murray and Andy Roberts against Pakistan at the 1975 World Cup.Shadab scored his maiden ODI century, making 113 off 96 balls in a match-winning effort that turned the game on its head as England let victory slip away.The win took Pakistan into the tri-series final.England had made a strong start while defending their target, with their bowlers working together to prevent Pakistan from building partnerships. Pakistan lost their top three batters — Fakhar Zaman (10 off 18), Saim Ayub (6 off 12) and Babar Azam (10 off 12) — inside the powerplay. England continued to take wickets and reduced the hosts to 154 for 9, but could not get the final breakthrough as Shadab and Rauf guided Pakistan to a memorable win in Lahore.Earlier, Pakistan captain and fast bowler Shaheen Shah Afridi took four wickets to restrict England to 241, despite a fighting century from Ben Duckett.England, who needed a win to stay in contention for the tri-series after losing their first two matches, struggled to recover after slipping to 19 for 3 on a batting-friendly pitch.Duckett scored 105 off 111 balls, while Sam Curran made 42 during a 93-run stand for the fifth wicket. Gus Atkinson added an unbeaten 36 towards the end of the innings.Shaheen finished with figures of 4 for 46, while ODI debutant Razaullah took 2 for 38 as England were bowled out in 46.4 overs.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Rajasthan look to break away from back-to-back draws against Uttarakhand as selection decisions come under scrutiny
articles.summary: Having secured back-to-back first-innings leads to accumulate six points from their opening two fixtures, Rajasthan face a pressing need to shift gears as
articles.body: Having secured back-to-back first-innings leads to accumulate six points from their opening two fixtures, Rajasthan face a pressing need to shift gears as they next take on Uttarakhand in their Ranji Trophy Group ‘D’ encounter in Dehradun starting Monday. Placed fourth on the points table, the Kartik Sharma-led side finds itself chasing the front-runners, Mumbai, Haryana, and Tamil Nadu, all of whom have capitalised on at least one outright victory to surge ahead.With draws against Tamil Nadu and Railways yielding only three points apiece, securing dominant, bonus-point wins has become paramount if the side wishes to bridge the gap. The squad received a timely boost ahead of the away match with the inclusion of seasoned seamer Aniket Choudhary. Sidelined for the first two matches due to a knee injury, Choudhary’s return injects vital experience into a talented yet youthful bowling attack. That added maturity will be crucial, particularly after injury to pacer Akash Singh.However, the build-up to the Dehradun fixture has been shadowed by mounting scrutiny off the field over the selection committee’s recent decisions. Questions have been raised regarding a series of perplexing moves, starting from the transitional phase after Manav Suthar's departure to India ‘A’ duties.While experienced campaigner Mahipal Lomror had stepped up as vice-captain, the selectors subsequently handed the reins to 20-year-old Kartik while retaining Lomror as deputy. The decision raised eyebrows given Lomror's proven track record as a leader.The turbulence deepened following the conclusion of the match against Railways, when Kunal Singh Rathore, returning from a ban imposed due to a dispute with fellow wicketkeeper-batter Rajkumar Saini, was straightaway instated as the new vice-captain, completely displacing Lomror from the leadership role.Compounding the unrest is the handling of another wicketkeeper-batter, Mukul Choudhary, whose journey through the tournament has been marked by a series of bizarre selection calls. A highly rated prospect who had recently impressed as a high-impact finisher in the IPL for the Lucknow Super Giants, Mukul's state campaign began on a turbulent note.After twisting his ankle just before the opening match, he was replaced in the playing XI by Sumit Godara. Yet, despite recovering and being fully fit for the second match, Mukul was completely left out of the team.The erratic shuffling peaked when the squad for the third match was initially announced with his name on the list, only for a revised squad to be released the very next day. Mukul was abruptly dropped and relegated to the Under-23 setup, with selectors bringing in Vishal Harsh to take his place.This constant back-and-forth shuffling has left the dressing room unsettled just as a crucial fixture beckons.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Ranji Trophy: Bengal look for hat-trick of wins as Kerala host table-toppers on seamer-friendly track
articles.summary: If momentum is important in sports, then both Kerala and Bengal will carry it in abundance when they face each other in an Elite Group C Ranji Trophy
articles.body: If momentum is important in sports, then both Kerala and Bengal will carry it in abundance when they face each other in an Elite Group C Ranji Trophy match at the KCA ground, Mangalapuram, in Thiruvananthapuram on Monday.Fresh from their innings victory against Odisha in their last match, Kerala will have a job in hand to stop an upbeat Bengal who will be looking for a hat-trick of wins after beating Delhi and Services to lie at the top of the table with 12 points in their group.However, Bengal will look for an improved show from their batters after they failed to put up enough runs on board against Services. It was their spinners who did the job for them then, but the KCA ground is unlikely to assist the spinners much. In that case Bengal might go in with three pacers, with Mohammed Shami once again taking up the new ball after the former India pacer sat out in the last game. He will expect good support from his brother Mohammed Kaif and Suraj Singh Jaiswal. Toss is likely to play an important role on a surface which offers early assistance to the pacers.Bengal coach Laxmi Ratan Shukla will look for more runs from the blades of Sudip Chatterjee and opener Ankur Pal as Bengal need to put up a competitive total against a good batting unit that features Sachin Baby, Vishnu Vinod and Mohammed Azharuddin. Much will depend on how the ever-dependent Jalaj Saxena contributes both with the ball and bat.Shahbaz Ahmed will once again play a key role for Bengal, after the all-rounder made an immediate impact on returning from an injury to play his first match in months against Services.However, the weather might play spoiler, with forecasts of occasional rain, which ruined the teams’ practice sessions, over the next few days. But the possibility of a complete washout is remote, and both sides are preparing for a stop-start game.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: From outranking the Fab Four to fight for his place: Rise, reign and the unraveling of Marnus Labuschagne
articles.summary: 'What the hell is that?' screamed Simon Katich from the commentary box as Marnus Labuschagne threw his wicket away in the second innings of the second
articles.body: 'What the hell is that?' screamed Simon Katich from the commentary box as Marnus Labuschagne threw his wicket away in the second innings of the second Test against South Africa. Australia had been forced to follow on and were only beginning to recover when their number three handed the hosts another opening.Labuschagne had batted patiently to reach 39 before dancing down the track to off-spinner Simon Harmer and attempting to hit him over the long-on boundary. He failed to clear the ropes and holed out to Marco Jansen.The brain fade laid waste to the 92-run partnership between Labuschagne and Travis Head as the visitors were trying to hang on for a draw.Australia eventually lost the Test by an innings and 31 runs.For Labuschagne, it was another failure to build on after getting the start. In four innings on the South Africa tour, in the country where he was born, the Australian batter has been dismissed in the thirties three times.For a batter who once seemed to have found a permanent home among the world's best, the struggle to convert starts into big scores has become a recurring problem of late.When Marnus ruled the world and outranked Fab FourAfter an unremarkable start to his career, he earned a place in Australia's squad for the 2019 Ashes in England. He was not among the biggest names in a team packed with established players, but the series would change his place in Australian cricket.At Lord's, Steve Smith was struck on the neck by a Jofra Archer bouncer and had to leave the field. Labuschagne came in as Test cricket's first concussion substitute, taking the place of a batter who was himself in the middle of a remarkable comeback. Under overcast skies, with England pressing for a win on the fifth day, Labuschagne scored 59 and helped Australia escape defeat.That innings proved to be a turning point. Over the following summer, Labuschagne went from a promising batter to one of the most consistent run-scorers in Test cricket.Against Pakistan, he scored 347 runs at an average of 173.50. He followed that with 549 runs at 91.50 against New Zealand, establishing himself as a key figure in Australia's Test batting line-up.His form continued in 2021, despite the challenges of playing through Covid restrictions. By the Boxing Day Test that year, Labuschagne had climbed to the top of the ICC Test batting rankings, ahead of Steve Smith, Joe Root, Virat Kohli and Kane Williamson — the four players Martin Crowe had famously grouped as the 'Fab Four'.A long way down from the topBetween 2019 and 2022, Labuschagne scored 2,990 runs in 50 innings at an average of 62.3. He hit 10 centuries and 13 fifties during that period.Since 2023, however, his returns have declined disastrously. In 66 innings between 2023 and 2026 so far, he has averaged 29.7, scoring 12 fifties and just one century. That hundred came in Manchester during the 2023 Ashes.The decline is particularly clear against pace bowling, once an area in which Labuschagne excelled. In 2020 and 2021, he averaged 76 and 74 against fast and medium-fast bowlers, respectively. From 2019 to 2022, his overall average against fast and medium-fast bowlers stood at 59.2.Since 2023, that number has dropped to just 28. In 2025, it fell to 18.(function(){function e(){window.addEventListener(`message`,function(e){if(e.data[`datawrapper-height`]!==void 0){var t=document.querySelectorAll(`iframe`);for(var n in e.data[`datawrapper-height`])for(var r=0,i;i=t[r];r++)if(i.contentWindow===e.source){var a=e.data[`datawrapper-height`][n]+`px`;i.style.height=a}}})}e()})();From Australia's safety net to its loose threadIn Test cricket, the number three position carries a particular mythologised lineage. It has been occupied by players such as Don Bradman and Ricky Ponting for Australia. Kumar Sangakkara played at first drop for Sri Lanka, Hashim Amla played that role for South Africa, and Rahul Dravid made that spot synonymous with himself for India.During his peak years, Labuschagne appeared to be Australia's long-term answer to the position.Among batters who played at least 15 innings at number three between 2019 and 2023, excluding players from Zimbabwe, Ireland and Afghanistan, Labuschagne averaged 65.85. Only Williamson, with an average of 67.16, was ahead of him.Since 2023, however, Labuschagne's average at number three has fallen to 31.72. Among the same group of batters who played at least 15 innings at the position between 2019 and 2023, he now has the lowest average.A number three, or any batter, can not make a hundred every time he walks out. There will be difficult conditions, good bowling and innings in which survival is the primary task. But the position demands a degree of reliability because the consequences of failure are often felt by the middle order.That is where Labuschagne's recent returns become particularly troubling. He is not consistently falling at the first hurdle. He is surviving long enough to create the expectation of a big innings, then failing to meet it.What is Labuschagne doing wrong?Labuschagne turned 32 in June, an age at which a Test batter would ordinarily expect to combine experience with technical and tactical maturity. He has played enough cricket to recognise different bowling plans and has spent years facing the world's best attacks. Yet his recent performances suggest that experience alone has not helped him find a solution.In the two Tests of the South Africa series, he has scored 37, 37, 14 and 39. Across his last eight innings, he has crossed 30 on five occasions but has repeatedly failed to go much further.Former Australia captain Greg Chappell believes Labuschagne's struggles may be part of a wider pattern that affects elite players after years at the top. In an article published in June 2025, Chappell described it as 'Elite Performance Decline Syndrome'.Speaking to Fox Sports last month, Chappell suggested that Labuschagne could be experiencing this phase of his career, with a decline in his average and influence accompanied by a loss of mental resilience.“Marnus is at the stage of his career that we all get to,” Chappell told Fox Sport last month.“What did I call it? I wrote an article: Elite Performance Decline Syndrome. You’ve got a finite number of innings in you and you sort of run out."That is one explanation, but there are also technical questions. Some observers believe Labuschagne is getting too front-on with his chest when defending, leaving him vulnerable to edges that carry to the slips. That was evident in the first innings of the second Test, when he edged Anrich Nortje to Simon Harmer.Australia captain Pat Cummins, however, has pointed towards decision-making rather than a fundamental flaw in technique. Labuschagne's attempt to hit Harmer over the boundary in the second innings was a case in point. Australia were batting to save the match, and the conditions, including a strong wind, offered little reason to take such a risk.“It’s certainly not a technique error. It’s ... maybe a couple of decision-making, some decisions (when) maybe the game demanded something a little bit different,” Cummins said.How much faith can a reputation buy?Labuschagne has been afforded more chances than most, but Australian cricket has a history of punishing batters whose judgement deserts them against South Africa.Damien Martyn's attempted airborne cover drive off Allan Donald in 1994 contributed to a six-year absence from the Test team. Brad Hodge, meanwhile, was dismissed by Andre Nel at the SCG in 2006 and subsequently lost his place.Labuschagne's situation is not identical to either case, but could he become the Proteas' third victim?Cummins has acknowledged that Labuschagne is doing the difficult part by reaching the 30s against an attack that has been making life uncomfortable for Australia's batters. But he has also made clear that those starts are not enough.“The balls are normally doing a fair bit. You got fresh bowlers, and he’s actually doing the hard bit (by) getting to 30s. I think he’s got to find a way to turn those into bigger scores (because) 30s aren’t going to win you too many matches," Cummins said after the second Test.Labuschagne, for his part, has expressed confidence in his ability to turn things around. “How can you not have faith?” he said before the South Africa tour in an interview with Fox Sports.He will hope Australia show faith in him for the third Test at Cape Town and that he can repay it with a big knock.However, another failure would strengthen the case for Australian selectors to reconsider his place in the side for New Zealand's tour of Australia in December.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Smriti Mandhana gives standing ovation as Harmanpreet Kaur slams eighth ODI century - Watch
articles.summary: Newly appointed India captain Smriti Mandhana was among those applauding Harmanpreet Kaur after the senior batter scored her eighth ODI century in the
articles.body: Newly appointed India captain Smriti Mandhana was among those applauding Harmanpreet Kaur after the senior batter scored her eighth ODI century in the second Women's ODI against Zimbabwe in Vadodara on Sunday.Harmanpreet reached the milestone in the 41st over, taking 101 balls to bring up her hundred. The Indian dressing room broke into applause, with Mandhana giving her a standing ovation. Harmanpreet kept her celebrations low-key, exchanging a handshake with Deepti Sharma before getting back to the job at hand.Harmanpreet went on to score 126 off 121 balls, while Deepti remained unbeaten on 106 off 86 deliveries as India recovered from an early collapse to post 328 for six.Harmanpreet was particularly effective on the off-side, finding the boundary with her cover drives and cuts. She shared a 153-run partnership with Deepti, who matched her with an attacking hundred to help India build a strong total.The match is part of the first-ever bilateral series between India and Zimbabwe, giving the visiting side an opportunity to compete against one of the top teams in women's cricket.India, however, did not get off to a good start. Mandhana, leading the side for the first time after her appointment as captain, mistimed a pull shot in the opening over and was dismissed cheaply. Shafali Verma followed soon after, getting caught at mid-wicket off Nomvelo Sibanda, who claimed her second wicket.Pratika Rawal then joined Harmanpreet to steady the innings. The pair added 124 runs before Rawal was caught at deep mid-wicket in the 23rd over after scoring 61 off 67 balls. Tejal Hasanbis also failed to connect with a slog sweep.Harmanpreet took charge from there, pacing her innings well on the way to her century. She also benefited from three dropped catches during her knock.The century was Harmanpreet's eighth in ODIs, and her innings came as she continued her career without the additional responsibility of leading the Indian team.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'I want to accept it': Harmanpreet Kaur embraces life beyond captaincy, says cricket continues to give her happiness
articles.summary: Harmanpreet Kaur wants to keep things simple and let her batting do the talking.
articles.body: Harmanpreet Kaur wants to keep things simple and let her batting do the talking. The India batter, who struck a magnificent 126 off 121 balls against Zimbabwe in the second ODI in Vadodara on Sunday, said she was focused on enjoying her cricket and accepting reality as she navigates a new phase in her career.Harmanpreet's century, which included 15 boundaries, helped India recover from an early setback and post a formidable 328/6. She shared a 153-run fifth-wicket partnership with Deepti Sharma, who remained unbeaten on 106, as India went on to register a commanding 121-run victory and take an unassailable 2-0 lead in the three-match series.Speaking after being named Player of the Match, Harmanpreet reiterated that enjoying her batting remained her priority, regardless of the circumstances surrounding her career.“I'm somebody who always likes to live life close to reality, and this is the reality now, and I just want to accept it in whatever way it is. At the same time, cricket is something which has always given me happiness, and batting is something which I've been enjoying throughout my career,” she said.“Today, and whenever I'm going to step in, I just want to enjoy my batting.”Harmanpreet, Pratika keep the approach simpleIndia were in trouble at 19 for two after captain Smriti Mandhana fell for a duck, but Harmanpreet and Pratika Rawal steadied the innings with a crucial partnership. Rawal scored 61 off 67 deliveries, while the pair added 124 runs for the third wicket to put India back on track.Harmanpreet said the plan was to respect Zimbabwe's good deliveries while capitalising on anything loose, with both batters clear about their approach in the ODI format.“Well, today we were playing an ODI format, and in ODI format, you have to act differently. That's what Pratika and I both decided, that we have to respect if they're bowling in the right areas, and at the same time, if we're getting any loose ball, we have to punish that,” she said.“I think it was a very simple and clear message we gave each other, and then just reacting.”The India batter's innings laid the foundation for a record-breaking stand with Deepti, who accelerated through the middle and death overs to bring up her century off 83 balls. Their 153-run partnership was India's highest for the fifth wicket in women's ODIs.‘You want to take responsibility for the team’Harmanpreet also stressed that her focus while batting remained on the team's needs rather than on her own position or role. Asked whether her current form made her miss captaincy less, she said she approached every innings with the same sense of responsibility.“When you're batting, you don't think these kinds of things. When you're batting, you're batting as a batter, and you want to take responsibility for the team,” she said.“I'm somebody who likes to take responsibility and bat according to the situation, and no matter whatever the situation is, I just want to enjoy myself.”Harmanpreet reveals she battled feverDespite spending nearly 45 overs at the crease in the afternoon heat, Harmanpreet revealed that she had not been at her best physically. The India batter said she had a mild fever the previous night and was struggling after returning to the field.“Yeah, definitely. I actually had a mild fever last night. That's why I was struggling when we came back to the field, and I just wanted to, you know, take some rest,” she said.She added that medication was helping and expressed hope that she would recover soon.“I think the painkillers, everything, are helping me, and hopefully I'll come back stronger,'' she signed-off.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'What did I do wrong?': Ex-India star reveals how being dropped from team pushed him into depression
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Being dropped from the Indian team was one of the toughest phases of Amit Mishra's cricket career.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Being dropped from the Indian team was one of the toughest phases of Amit Mishra's cricket career. The former India leg-spinner has revealed that he battled depression for 18 months because he could not understand why he was not getting chances to play for the country.Mishra made his international debut in 2003. However, he soon found himself out of the Indian team. He was also not picked for some domestic tournaments. Despite continuing to play cricket, he kept wondering why he was being left out.Speaking to former India batter Aakash Chopra, Mishra opened up about how the setback affected him.“I went into depression for a year and a half. I kept thinking about what my mistake was. I was playing everywhere, but the only question in my mind was that, ‘what did I do wrong?’" Mishra said.A selector's advice helped Amit MishraMishra was also left out of the Duleep Trophy and the India A zonal setup. He struggled to understand why he was not getting opportunities until a selector spoke to him about his performances.“Then a selector told me that I was not performing. I sat down and thought, and I understood that I was thinking of playing for India itself but not performing in domestic cricket," he recalled.The selector's words made Mishra think about his approach. He realised that he was thinking too much about returning to the Indian team and not focusing enough on performing in domestic cricket.Mishra returned to domestic circuit, worked on his game, and his performances eventually helped him return to the Indian team in 2008, almost five years after his debut.He went on to play 22 Tests, 36 ODIs and 10 T20Is for India. He claimed taking 156 wickets across the three formats.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'I don't think we can reveal on live TV': Shadab Khan on chat with Haris Rauf
articles.summary: Pakistan all-rounder Shadab Khan had plenty to say about his conversation with Haris Rauf during their match-winning partnership against England.
articles.body: Pakistan all-rounder Shadab Khan had plenty to say about his conversation with Haris Rauf during their match-winning partnership against England. After guiding Pakistan to a thrilling one-wicket win in Lahore on Sunday, Shadab revealed that the two were talking more about things other than cricket.“He was explaining things to me more than I was explaining things to him. He was saying things along the way that I don't think we can reveal on live TV. I think we had a lot of fun moments and really enjoyed ourselves. We were talking more about other things than cricket,” Shadab said after being named Player of the Match.Their conversation seemed to work wonders as Pakistan pulled off a remarkable comeback. Chasing 242, the hosts were struggling at 154-9 before Shadab and Rauf joined hands to take the team home.Shadab, Rauf script record partnershipShadab remained unbeaten on 113, while Rauf scored seven not out off 19 balls. The pair added 89 runs for the last wicket, the highest partnership for the final wicket in a successful ODI run chase.Pakistan needed a strong finish after England's bowlers had put them on the back foot. Shadab struck 13 fours and five sixes to lead the fightback, while Rauf played a crucial supporting role.Shadab was given out lbw with Pakistan needing 21 runs to win. However, he reviewed the decision and survived after replays showed an inside edge.Reflecting on the partnership, Shadab said Rauf deserved more credit for helping Pakistan cross the finish line.“Obviously, you only enjoy an innings when the team wins. So, I'm very happy that I played that innings and we won the match. I think Haris deserves more credit than me because, obviously, tailenders at that position are always keen to hit sixes. The way I was guiding him, or he was guiding me, we managed to put together a good partnership.”Shadab reveals what kept him going at 154-9Pakistan looked close to defeat when Shadab found himself with the last man at the crease. However, the all-rounder said he kept believing that he could finish the job.“Obviously, I think you just go with the flow. When I made my comeback in the last series, there was an innings against Australia where I kept going until the end, but I couldn't win the match. So the idea was to keep believing. The conditions were a little different today, with dew coming in. I also felt their bowling was under a bit of pressure, given how things had gone in the previous match. I thought that if we could put them under pressure, they might end up bowling in areas that suited my game.”Afridi's four wickets put England under pressureEarlier, England were bowled out for 241 in 46.4 overs after Ben Duckett scored a composed 105. Shaheen Shah Afridi led Pakistan's bowling attack with four wickets for 46 runs.Afridi struck in the first over to dismiss Tom Banton and removed Joe Root in the third. Haris Rauf then sent Jordan Cox back as England slipped to 52-4.Duckett and Sam Curran rebuilt the innings with a 93-run partnership for the fifth wicket. Curran scored 42 before becoming Afridi's third victim. Jamie Overton helped England cross 200, while Gus Atkinson remained unbeaten on 36.Pakistan's chase also got off to a poor start as Fakhar Zaman and Babar Azam fell for 10 each. Saad Baig scored a quick 32 off 22 balls, while Salman Ali Agha made 26, but Pakistan continued to lose wickets.Shadab arrived at the crease in the 24th over with Pakistan at 103-6. His unbeaten century eventually turned the match around and secured a place for the hosts in the tri-series final.The defeat was England's third consecutive loss in the tri-series. They had earlier suffered a heavy blow when Sri Lanka chased down 430 with one ball remaining, completing the second-highest successful run chase in ODI history.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: PAK vs ENG: Drama in Lahore! Shadab Khan walks off, England celebrate, then comes a twist - WATCH
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: For a few moments at Lahore's Gaddafi Stadium, it seemed Pakistan had lost the match.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: For a few moments at Lahore's Gaddafi Stadium, it seemed Pakistan had lost the match. England's players had started celebrating, handshakes were exchanged and Shadab Khan looked devastated. But a review changed everything, and the hosts went on to pull off a stunning one-wicket victory in the ODI tri-series on Sunday.Pakistan were chasing 242 and had slipped to 154-9. With just one wicket left, defeat looked certain. Then Shadab and Haris Rauf produced a remarkable fightback, taking Pakistan home and securing their place in the final.Shadab remained unbeaten on 113, but his innings had one moment that could have ended the contest before its dramatic finish.Shadab walks away, but the review saves PakistanThe drama unfolded in the 45th over when Gus Atkinson trapped Shadab on the pads. The bowler appealed, and the umpire raised his finger. Shadab appeared to accept his fate and began walking away.England's players thought they had won. Some started shaking hands, while the television briefly flashed a result showing England winning by 20 runs.Shadab was clearly upset. He struck his bat against the ground and went down on his haunches. Joe Root and Harry Brook approached him to shake hands as other England players began celebrating.But Shadab decided to review the decision, and the replays changed the mood inside the stadium. UltraEdge showed a spike, confirming that the ball had touched his bat before hitting his pad.The decision was overturned, and the crowd erupted. Shadab was given another chance to finish the match, while England's players looked stunned. Rauf, who had put his hand on his head during the tense moment, also watched in disbelief.Shadab responded with a fist pump. Pakistan's hopes were alive again, and the match continued.Shadab and Rauf pull off an incredible comebackWhen Rauf joined Shadab in the 34th over, Pakistan were struggling at 154-9. England needed only one more wicket, but the last pair refused to surrender.Shadab took responsibility for the chase, scoring quickly and protecting Rauf from facing too many deliveries. He kept most of the strike and continued to put pressure on England's bowlers.Playing his first match of the tournament, Shadab smashed 113 not out off 96 balls, with 12 fours and five sixes. Rauf supported him with an unbeaten seven off 19 deliveries.Their 89-run partnership was the highest for the 10th wicket in a successful ODI run chase.Shadab brought up his maiden ODI century with a late cut off Atkinson and followed it with a six over long-off. Pakistan needed only three runs from the final three overs when Rauf struck the winning boundary off Henry Crocombe.Pakistan finished on 243-9 in 47.1 overs to complete a victory few would have expected when their ninth wicket fell.Afridi strikes early as England are bowled out for 241Earlier, England were dismissed for 241 in 46.4 overs after being asked to bat first. Ben Duckett top-scored with 105 off 111 balls, hitting 10 fours and two sixes.Shaheen Shah Afridi put England under pressure from the start. He dismissed Tom Banton in the first over and Joe Root in the third, before Rauf removed Jordan Cox. England were soon reduced to 52-4.Duckett and Sam Curran then gave the innings some stability, adding 93 runs for the fifth wicket. Curran scored 42 off 52 balls before Afridi dismissed him, completing his third wicket of the innings.Afridi finished with 4-46 as England continued to lose wickets. They slipped to 201-9 before Gus Atkinson, who remained unbeaten on 36, helped them reach 241.Despite Duckett's century and Atkinson's late contribution, England's total was not enough to stop Pakistan's remarkable chase.England come close, but Pakistan survivePakistan also struggled with the bat. Fakhar Zaman and Babar Azam scored 10 each, while Saim Ayub managed only six. Jamie Overton took two catches in the slips to dismiss Fakhar and Saim, while Atkinson bowled Babar.Saad Baig added a quick 32 off 22 balls, and Salman Ali Agha scored 26. But England continued to take wickets, with Overton finishing with 3-43 and Liam Dawson claiming 2-30.At 154-9, England were firmly in control. However, Shadab's counter-attack, Rauf's support and the crucial review turned the match on its head.Pakistan book a place in the finalThe victory secured Pakistan's place in the ODI tri-series final. They will play Sri Lanka in their last league match on Tuesday, having beaten them by 37 runs in the opening game.England, meanwhile, suffered their third consecutive defeat. They had earlier lost to Pakistan by 87 runs and then suffered a heartbreaking loss against Sri Lanka, who chased down 430 with one ball remaining.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Ranji Trophy: Karnataka look to turn the corner
articles.summary: MYSURU: The city is still glowing in the afterglow of Dasara, with the lights from the 11-day festivities continuing to bathe the heritage city in gold.
articles.body: MYSURU: The city is still glowing in the afterglow of Dasara, with the lights from the 11-day festivities continuing to bathe the heritage city in gold. Karnataka will hope some of that festive cheer rubs off on their Ranji Trophy campaign when they take on a struggling Tripura at the SDNRW Stadium on Monday.The former champions have managed just two points from as many matches and sit sixth in the eight-team Group B. Against Andhra and Saurashtra, they let opportunities slip, conceding first-innings leads in contests where they could have collected at least three points.A combination of shortcomings has left Karnataka searching for answers. Often their batters have failed to convert promising starts or have fallen to soft dismissals. The bowling, too, has lacked penetration despite the return of experienced pacers Vidwath Kaverappa and Vyshak Vijaykumar. Fielding remains another concern, with dropped catches and misfields proving costly against Saurashtra.Karnataka are a team in transition, with several rookies still finding their feet. However, debutants Manvanth Kumar and Madhav Bajaj have shown enough promise to suggest that the new crop can make a difference.Tripura, who arrive after two heavy defeats — an innings and 40 runs against Hyderabad and a nine-wicket loss to Assam — offer Karnataka an opportunity to get their campaign back on track. But the hosts will need a more complete performance to make it count.The opening partnership is one area that demands immediate attention. Karnataka have used three different opening combinations across four innings due to non-availability of players, with first-wicket stands of 9, 18, 12 and 45. If they bat first, seeing off the new ball and building a substantial partnership in the opening hour will be crucial. The batting order is yet to fire collectively, and this fixture offers a chance to find its rhythm.Overcast conditions expected on the opening day could assist the pacers. Karnataka’s bowlers will need to maintain disciplined lengths and strike early, rather than allow Tripura’s batters to settle.Karnataka fielded just one spinner against Saurashtra at the KSCA Alur Stadium last week. They could consider strengthening that area and bring in left-arm spinner Shikhar Shetty.Stand-in captain Shreyas Gopal remains confident that the team’s efforts will soon translate into results.“The thought process for a Karnataka team is always to win. Unfortunately, we missed out on two points in both games, but I’m extremely proud of the way we are putting the opposition under pressure on batting-friendly wickets. We are giving ourselves a chance, and that good effort will show in the games to follow,” he said.Tripura, meanwhile, have struggled to come together as a batting unit despite having seasoned players such as India Test cricketer Hanuma Vihari and Mandeep Singh. Captain Manisankar Murasingh will be central to their hopes, leading the bowling attack while also arriving in form with the bat after scoring a quickfire century against Assam.For Karnataka, the equation is simple: against an opponent low on confidence, they need to turn promising passages of play into a winning performance.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Ranji Trophy: Wary Delhi eye winning return against Jharkhand
articles.summary: KOLKATA: With just two rounds remaining before the Ranji Trophy pauses for the BCCI’s white-ball competitions, Jharkhand will be looking to play an
articles.body: KOLKATA: With just two rounds remaining before the Ranji Trophy pauses for the BCCI’s white-ball competitions, Jharkhand will be looking to play an aggressive brand of cricket and maximise their points haul when they take on Delhi in their Elite Group C clash at JSCA International Cricket Stadium in Ranchi starting Monday.Having collected four points from their opening two matches, Jharkhand find themselves in the middle of a tightly-packed group and know that a strong finish to the first phase could significantly boost their qualification hopes.“We need points now,” Jharkhand coach Ratan Kumar told TOI ahead of the contest. “Delhi are a good batting side, a balanced side and have always been a challenging team. Our focus is that we go all out in this match because good points here will help us going forward.”Delhi, led by Ayush Badoni, arrive with just three points from two games and will also see the fixture as an opportunity to move up the table. Badoni and Priyansh Arya are the visitors’ biggest batting threats after producing massive scores in the drawn match against Gujarat, with Arya falling agonisingly short of a double century on 199 and Badoni hammering 217.Jharkhand began their campaign by securing three points against Kerala after taking a first-innings lead at home before fighting hard for a draw against Maharashtra in Pune. Young opener Shikhar Mohan starred in that escape act with a century in the second innings, but the hosts will be without him this week after his maiden India A call-up for the final two unofficial Tests in New Zealand.While Mohan’s absence leaves a sizeable void at the top, Ratan is confident others can step up.“Shikhar was batting very well and has gone for India duty. But we cannot keep thinking about the player who is not there. The boys who get opportunities now have to make them count,” he said.Aryaman Sen is expected to be among the contenders to fill the opening slot, while veteran batter Kumar Deobrat is also under consideration. The coach also backed opener Sharandeep Singh, whose highest score this season remains 33.“He has not got the returns he would have wanted in the first two matches, but we have full confidence in him,” Ratan said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Just one run short! Devdutt Padikkal falls for 199; reaction to umpire goes viral - WATCH
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Devdutt Padikkal was left heartbroken after missing out on a double century by just one run on Day 3 of the first unofficial Test between India
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Devdutt Padikkal was left heartbroken after missing out on a double century by just one run on Day 3 of the first unofficial Test between India A and New Zealand A at the Bert Sutcliffe Oval in Lincoln.The left-hander looked shocked when umpire raised his finger after New Zealand A appealed for a catch behind off Zak Gibson. Padikkal stood on the pitch for a few moments, looking at the umpire and signalling that the ball had gone down the leg side and appeared to have brushed his pads.But the decision went against him, forcing him to walk back to the pavilion on 199. He shook his head in disappointment as he left the field, while Yash Rathod walked up to him and tapped him on the shoulder to acknowledge his effort.Gibson bowled a delivery down the leg side, and Padikkal tried to clip it towards the leg side but missed. The ball appeared to brush his pads before settling into wicketkeeper Mitchell Hay's gloves. There was a sound as the ball passed the bat, but Padikkal seemed convinced that it had not come off his bat. The appeal did not appear particularly strong, yet the umpire raised his finger.Padikkal immediately looked towards the umpire in disbelief and gestured to show how far the ball was from his bat. He remained on the pitch briefly, clearly unhappy with the decision, before making his way back.His innings ended at 199 off 248 balls, including 24 fours and three sixes. It was a fine knock under pressure, but the manner and timing of his dismissal made the end particularly painful.Padikkal fights back after India A lose early wicketsIndia A had been bowled out for just 113 in the first innings and needed a strong response. However, their openers failed again, with Yashasvi Jaiswal and KL Rahul falling early in the second innings. India A were reduced to 10 for two, leaving the team in trouble once more.Padikkal then took charge and helped India A recover from the early collapse.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: IND vs NZ: Ishan Kishan ruled out of third T20I against New Zealand
articles.summary: Ishan Kishan will miss the third T20 International against New Zealand as he continues to recover from a thigh injury, the BCCI confirmed on Monday.
articles.body: Ishan Kishan will miss the third T20 International against New Zealand as he continues to recover from a thigh injury, the BCCI confirmed on Monday.The wicketkeeper-batter suffered a right adductor strain during the first T20I last week. He also missed the second match and has not yet regained full match fitness.The BCCI said Kishan was making progress but was not ready to return to action."Ishan Kishan is recovering well from his low grade right adductor strain, which he sustained during the first T20I of the series against New Zealand," BCCI said in a statement."He is yet to regain match fitness and is ruled out of the third T20I to be played on October 27, 2026 in Wellington. The BCCI Medical Team is monitoring Ishan's progress. Kumar Kushagra will continue to be with the team for the third T20I," the statement said.The right adductor muscles are located on the inner side of the thigh and help with leg movement.Kishan's absence gave teenage batting sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi an opportunity in the playing XI for the second T20I.India had also brought in uncapped wicketkeeper-batter Kumar Kushagra as cover for the injured Kishan. The BCCI has confirmed that Kushagra will remain with the squad for the third match.India have won the first two matches and lead the five-match series 2-0. The third T20I will be played in Wellington on October 27.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: IND A vs NZ A, 1st unofficial Test: Devdutt Padikkal's 199, Washington Sundar's fifty put India A in control against New Zealand A
articles.summary: India A put themselves in a strong position in the first unofficial Test against New Zealand A after a solid batting effort on Day 3 in Lincoln on Monday.
articles.body: India A put themselves in a strong position in the first unofficial Test against New Zealand A after a solid batting effort on Day 3 in Lincoln on Monday. They reached 488 for 8 in their second innings, taking their overall lead to 284 runs before bad light brought an early end to the day's play.Devdutt Padikkal led the recovery with a brilliant 199, missing out on a double century by just one run. Washington Sundar remained unbeaten on 51 as India A strengthened their position after being dismissed for just 113 in the first innings.Padikkal's superb knock ended at 199 off 248 balls, including 24 fours and three sixes. He was given out caught behind off Zak Gibson while attempting to play a delivery down the leg side. The left-hander looked surprised by the decision and had to leave just one run short of a double century.Rathod and Sundar keep the runs comingRathod made a valuable 66 off 72 balls, hitting eight fours. He helped India A extend their lead before falling to Foxcroft shortly after tea, caught behind by wicketkeeper Mitchell Hay.Anshul Kamboj added 23 off 36 balls but was bowled by Jayden Lennox. Auqib Nabi then scored 38 off 63 deliveries, striking three fours and two sixes, before Clarke dismissed him.Sundar stayed at the crease and reached his 13th first-class half-century. He was unbeaten on 51 off 75 balls, with six fours, at stumps. His contribution helped India A push their lead beyond 250 runs.India A ended the day at 488 for 8 after 119 overs. Akash Deep was yet to score, while Mukesh Choudhary was still to bat.Will India A declare on Day 4?With a 284-run lead and two wickets remaining, India A must decide whether to declare early on Tuesday or add more runs before asking New Zealand A to bat again.Rain is forecast for the fourth day, which could affect their plans. India A may want to leave enough time for their bowlers to take 10 wickets, but extending their lead would also give them greater control over the match.New Zealand A were bowled out for 317 in their first innings, giving India A a 204-run advantage before the start of their second innings. articles.title: 'We've got a bulletproof plan for everyone, including Jasprit Bumrah': Indian bowling coach Morne Morkel on workload issue
articles.summary: India are planning to keep a separate group of bowlers in New Zealand as backup for the two-match Test series next month.
articles.body: India are planning to keep a separate group of bowlers in New Zealand as backup for the two-match Test series next month.Bowling coach Morne Morkel said on Monday that the move is part of a carefully planned strategy to manage the bowlers’ workload during a demanding tour featuring five T20Is, five ODIs and two Tests.The Test series begins on November 19, just four days after the five-match ODI series ends, making workload management important for the team.Morkel said the team would decide on its bowling combination closer to the series after assessing the conditions in New Zealand."We are planning a group of bowlers that we would like to potentially stay behind as cover because of the schedule. Closer to the time, once we get a better understanding of the conditions at this time of the year, we'll get a clear picture regarding the make-up of our bowling unit," Morkel said.Backing Arshdeep’s credentials, the bowling coach added, "On paper and in the back of our minds, there is a nice group of bowlers that can suit all conditions, and Arshdeep is definitely in that conversation."He's a guy that always works hard and ticks all the boxes, so if needed with the red ball, I'm pretty sure he'll be fine," the former South African fast bowler added.Rotation plan to prevent burnoutIndia have been preparing their workload strategy for months, with some players already featuring for the India A side to build their readiness for red-ball cricket. The team also plans to rotate bowlers during the ODIs so they can gain match practice and gradually prepare for the Tests."Every bowler is clear on what is expected of them in terms of workload and bowling. As you are aware, a couple of guys are playing in the A-side to get ready for red-ball cricket," Morkel added.Explaining the preparations, he said, "In the 50-over format, we will also rotate and give guys the game time needed to prepare for the Test matches. We've got a bulletproof plan at the moment in terms of how we mapped everything out, but unfortunately, not everything always goes according to plan."The back-up and combinations we have are all in place and ready in terms of rotation, making sure everyone, including Jasprit Bumrah all the way down, is ready for the first red-ball Test and the 50-over games," Morkel said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 99 runs leaked in 2 T20Is! Bhuvneshwar Kumar gets a message from Morne Morkel
articles.summary: India bowling coach Morne Morkel has asked Bhuvneshwar Kumar to stay calm, ignore outside pressure and focus on his own game as the experienced fast
articles.body: India bowling coach Morne Morkel has asked Bhuvneshwar Kumar to stay calm, ignore outside pressure and focus on his own game as the experienced fast bowler tries to find his rhythm after returning to the T20I team following a four-year gap.Bhuvneshwar's comeback has not gone as planned. The 36-year-old conceded 49 runs in the first T20I against New Zealand and 50 in the second, taking just one wicket across the two matches. His economy rate of 12.37 has been the highest among India's bowlers in the series.With India trailing 0-2 in the five-match series, Morkel has backed the veteran pacer to improve as he gets more opportunities on the field.'Block the expectation factor out'Morkel said Bhuvneshwar would naturally face expectations after returning to the international stage following four years away from the T20I side. He also pointed to the bowler's strong performances in the IPL."I've got a lot of sympathy for his return. There will be expectations after four years to come back. He has done exceptionally well in the IPL and bowled really well," Morkel said on the eve of the third T20I.The bowling coach said preparing for international cricket was not easy, especially when a player had limited time to get ready before the series."One challenge is to block the expectation factor out. Two, leading into selection, he trained for a month, but playing international cricket is a different beast where the margins are small. He had to come in with limited training because of the schedule to get himself ready."Bhuvneshwar played an important role in Royal Challengers Bengaluru's back-to-back IPL titles. He took 17 wickets in the 2025 season and followed that up with 28 wickets in 2026.Morkel backs Bhuvneshwar to find his rhythmDespite the expensive outings in the first two matches, Morkel believes Bhuvneshwar has the skills and experience needed to bounce back. He urged the bowler not to put himself under pressure to deliver immediately."The skill and his experience, everything is there. But at the end of the day, we have to respect the game of cricket and you have to be able to allow him to just find his feet in some of the games."Morkel said his message to Bhuvneshwar had been simple from the moment the pacer joined the squad."And for me, that has been the message from the start when he joined the squad, don't chase anything. Just be you."He added that the bowler should focus on his game rather than worry about what others expected from him."Yes, there will be expectations. But every game you'll get better and every game you'll find your rhythm. So let's not think about any outside noises.
